A History of Oerik 
Book 1 
Part 24
   In the year -53 SD a baby girl was born to a Lowly One family in the servitude of a moderately well off household in the Singing Lands.
    Their masters, kinder than most elves, and rather sympathetic to their slaves, treated the Lowly Ones as compassionately as they felt able. The baby's father could actually read and write and performed the task of secretary.
The girl was called Win-Daled and was exceptionally smart.  This would ordinarily be a problem as the Singing Ones regularly sent the more clever Lowly Ones to the torture parks, but instead Win- Daled's natural intelligence was encouraged, which was quite brave of the elven family, who secretly supported emancipation.
   While she was four, Win-Daled got to play with the young Ye'Cind, a fifty year old elfling with a mischievous streak who was the youngest member of the elven family.
   Ye'Cind was as musically gifted as a typical Singing One but her actual voice was horrible.  She had a perfect pitch, but the harsh honking sound that came out of her throat was repugnant.  Ye'Cind loved to make animal calls and she hooted with laughter whenever she managed to scare Win-Daled with her griffin cries. Fortunately, most of the time the two of them got on extremely well, and would chat and laugh with each other frequently.
   One day, Ye'Cind's father managed to form a complex trading scheme that included the Crystalmist dwarves, the Wind Dukes to.the northwest, and the Blemu Confederation.He would need to gate to various places to supervise and oversee the trading to make sure everything was in order.  
Ye' Cind's mother was a politician who was often working at the Senate or attending concerts or parties, always attempting to swing other Singing Ones to her point of view, which involved more rights for the Lowly Ones as well as reforming to a more centralised government.
 There was never enough time for her or her husband  to manage the welfare and education of Ye'Cind as well as they would want, and they both feared she would turn out half wild, so 
it was agreed that her husband would take Ye'Cind with him on his trading meetings, and his secretary would be allowed to take Win-Daled along too,, as Ye'Cind and Win-Daled were almost inseparable. See less

    Amongst the broad trees of the southern Adri forest (now part of the Grandwood), a majestic unicorn dug about in the top soil for delicious dandelion roots. Then, it quickly raised its head, the horn jutting out of its forehead shining a brilliant magenta. Something bad was around, but where...
   A great brown, barreling beast, armoured and fanged and muscular, burst up from under the unicorn and dragged it down with its shark-like jaws. A bulette had made itself a lair in the forest and had decided that unicorns were most delicious. 
   Heward, who was checking a rabbit trap, saw the eruptive scene and was incensed. Unicorns were sacred animals and Heward decided that the horrible monster must have ascended from the Underworld. The young Flan warrior went off and found his friends, the brilliant Win-Daled and the silvery elven mage Ye'Cind. Heward told them what he saw and the three friends resolved  to hunt down the bulette. 
   Some nearby pixies had seen the monster emerge from the ground and slake its thirst  at a nearby creek. It had only just burrowed down back into the earth.  The pixies showed them the spot, then flew up into the trees to watch the coming exciitement.
   Ye'Cind could see the dirt mound created by the bulette.  Heward was all for diving under the ground after it but Win-Daled thought that a really stupid idea. Instead they tracked around until they found a couple of unicorns nibbling plants on a shady hillock.  Ye'Cind wanted to warn the unicorns away but Win-Daled thought it better to wait.  Ye'Cind said that was callous and began neighing in unicorn fashion and stamping the ground.  
   Heward felt a rumble travelling underneath his feet and drew his sword but  the Bulette moved past him and  burst up underneath Ye'Cind, throwing her into the air.  She tumbled to the ground about twenty yards away and as she spat blood out of her mouth she thought she saw a great flash emanate from Win-Daled that was immediately followed by a loud crack . Bits of Bullette rained everywhere. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 1 
Part 31
-20SD
Demon worshippers from MaiYuan spread their philosophy to Eastern Oerik which attracted interest amongst diverse peoples. Demonic shrines popped up in quiet, hidden away places where congregants would secretly  go to dabble in necromancy, demonology and other evil Magicks. 
   The Celenian elves became very much enamoured with the cults of the MaiYuan, the Empire of Merchants across the seas, as did the Singing Ones.
   A number of Flan formed small little cults where they plotted small little plans, despite the Blemu anathema to such worship. The Blemu leadership was actually quite worried, because demon worship and the philosophy of rampant hedonism was close to their own beliefs, but the Blemu tempered their Fey  hedonism with compassion and empathy.
   Win -Daled, Ye'Cind and Heward, the three Heroes, were tasked with winkling out these hidden shrines of Evil, but when ideas take hold and when they promote power without consequence, new weeds spring up as  just asothers are cut down. Win-Daled reasoned that unless the evil could be eliminated at the source, the Demon cults would continue to grasp and swallow in the good people of Eastern Oerik. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 1 
Part 32
   How were the demons to be defeated? Travel into the Abyss and confront them in their lair? Suicidal, besides how would they get there? Heward shrugged, Win-Daled was pretty good at magic, surely she had a spell? Ye'Cind snorted with good humour, extra-planar travel was rare and the methods were mostly secret. Should Win-Daled ask a dragon for the formula?
   The three Heroes ended their meal bickering vehemently.
.  
   Eventually, it was decided that Heward would travel to the Singing Lands and look for any weaknesses that could be exploited.  What sort of weaknesses? Something that might cause a rift between the elves and the demons, or perhaps weaken the cohesion in their society.  Heward was the best fit for the job because as an outsider, neither a Singing One like Ye'Cind or a Lowly One  like Win-Daled,  Heward would more likely be able to mix with either class. Heward was a Flan, tanned with brown wavy hair and broad shoulders. His ancestors were a little mysterious, there were rumours one of his grandmother's was part nymph and one of his cousins had pointy ears like an elf. All in all, Heward made a perfect travelling merchant.
   The Singing Lands had become openly debauched. The Singing Ones lived for pleasure, a dark pleasure that was destructive. Torture Clubs were commonplace, and noxious herbs were imbibed before the corrupt elves engaged in demonic sacrifices involving unwilling slaves. Over indulgence in food and drink was de riguer, and the Singing Ones spent less and less time actually working.
   Work became the burden of the Lowly Ones. Everything needed to be done was left for these slaves. Supervision used to be strict, but as hedonism took over, much of the overseeing was done by the Lowly Ones themselves. Consequently, many tasks were left undone or badly done, and many Lowly Ones were able to hide away and form lucrative thieving networks. 
   The only jobs still enthusiastically managed by the Singing Ones were the secret police, but even they couldn't be everywhere. Sometimes they did uncover thief dens but there were so many underground, hidden places for the Lowly Ones to gather, and with the majority of Singing Ones being apathetic, the Lowly Ones were actually developing a strong counter culture.
   Heward moved through the run down streets, admiring the architecture and the spontaneous singing that would erupt when more than three Singing Ones gathered together. He saw the occasional demon or daemon trudging along or bouncing about with flapping bat wings, but they ignored him presumably because they gained their satiation in the Torture Clubs and temples.
 Heward had managed to get the name of a local thief guild master. Hopefully he would be able to make contact. See less

Part 40
Dweomyne sang in three octaves at once.  The sonic blast threw Win-Daled and Ye'Cind to the floor. Dweomyne leapt off her throne and flew into the air, her whip arcing backward ready to lash.  
   Winded and hands scorching, Ye'Cind  unrolled another spell from the smoking Scroll of Vile Darkness and frantically began mouthing the words.  
   Mocinlyte the succubus, hearing the commotion from the adjacent chamber, burst into the room, determined to help her mistress. She tore at  Win-Daled, but the Lowly One cooly raised a hand and turned her to ice. The translucent demoness toppled over and  shattered.
     The Whip Lady danced forward, still singing, and flicked her whip across  Ye'Cind, but Heward was there again and took the brunt, his cheek slicing open  Grimacing with pain, he attempted to sever the whip with his sword but the magical weapon unnaturally angled away. Quick as a leopard, Dweomyne  drew a serrated dagger from her robe, whip curling impatiently in her other hand.  With a sonic roar she descended upon Heward and furiously struck at him.  Heward struggled  with the dagger and the wicked blade slid across the air just missing his throat. 
   He swung his own weapon and caught Dweomyne in her side as her whip curled around his thigh. The Whip Lady over balanced and fell but pulled Heward down with her.  
   An  eldritch flame of violet streaked from Ye'Cind's scroll and streamed into the Whip Lady's mouth, rushing down into her throatt. She attempted to blast it away with song but her oesephogeous filled with flame.
   Now Dweomyne felt the writhing pain she had inflicted upon so many as the unholy fire roasted her from the inside. Even so, she managed to stagger up and flick her whip, tearing the Scroll of Vile Darkness off Ye'Cind and flinging it towards her.
 Heward reached out and brushed the scroll with his fingers, but it hissed at him and sparked angrily.
The Whip Lady bent down and took  the spitting scroll into her hands. She shuddered and convulsed as the fire rolled out of her throat  and back into the scroll. The pain faded and Dweomyne broke into a cruel smile. She would survive yet! 
 But just as she moved to shape a spell that would turn the trio into dust,  another blue light streaked out  from Win-Daled and  encircled her , holding her off. The Scroll of Vile Darkness, enraged, burst into blinding whiteness that blew out a hole in the wall. With one final spark, the scroll fled the Material Universe, taking Dweomyne with it.  As the ruler of the Singing Ones dematerialised, the Whip Lady swung her whip around again, catching Win-Daled around the leg, bringing her down and spoiling the spell.
    Yet, as the whip wound around Win-Daled, it left  Dweomyne's grip, who was now fully insubstantial. The whip was left on Oerth as the Whip Lady fell through the Astral Plane and plunged into the Abyss.
   Ye' Cind, Heward and Win-Daled were too injured and weary to be happy, yet they looked at each other with satisfaction. Dweomyne was gone, and their family was avenged. Win-Daled carefully unwrapped the whip from off her legs, wincing. It thrummed with power as she turned it over in her hands, trying to decipher the magic glyphs etched into the straps. See less

A History of Oerik
Book 1 
Part 44
20's SD
  Several nations made up the lands of Eastern Oerik.
   The lands surrounding and incorporating the Adri/Grandwood forest was the elven kingdom of Blemu, but with numerous autonomous villages and towns  occupied by Flan.
    Rangers and druids congregated here and human wizard colleges were established.
   West of Blemu were three small states, two Flan and one, set within the Flinty hills, dwarvish. These states were granted their liberty the Blemu sovereign.
   South of the Thelly river were the home of Dwarven clans  collectively known as HardThistle.  Flan villages also dotted this region, mostly at peace with the dwur.
At the mouth of the Vast swamp were wild lands dominated by humanoids and monsters.
   Much of the west, including what is now Furyondy, the Shield Lands, Nyrond and Celene,  and the Celadon, Dim, Suss and Gambodge forests, was the burgeoning Empire of Celene. The Flan were serfs and servants and slaves.
   East of Blemu in what is now North Province, were numerous tiny kinglets of Flan war chiefs,  effectively a lawless society.  They grew wealthy  trading with the sea elves who controlled all the major islands of what is now the Aerdi sea, but spent most of their time in using their riches to gain power for themselves over the other chiefs.
   West of Celene were Dwur and Sheldar hunter, gatherers. Primarily good, but hard hearted, they defended the realms against Celenian incursions. They spoke a mixture of different dialects to those east of the Lortmils.  
   South of lake Quag and west of the sylvan lands of the Vesve in what is now Perrenland, were a hidden realm of Flan who had contacts with MaiYuan and studied demonology.  Calling themselves the Ur-Flan (great Flan). this evil theocracy seeped slowly through Oerik like a dripping tap.
To the north of Oerik were great hosts of humanoids coexisting with large barbarian tribes. 
   The great ranges of the Barrier Peaks, the Crystalmists and the Sulhauts that bordered Western Oerik were dominated by the mountain dwarves,, wisely ruled by the beneficent and steady Moradin, the Soul Forger,: the God King for all dwur kind. See less

29-55 SD
   Win-Daled was reaching the end of her mortal life.  She had ruled Risewater, home of the Suloise, for many years and the population had  increased,  with further settlements to the North and West.. But the East was off limits, too close to the  Singing Lands.
   Most of her tenure as Suel Chief had been relatively easy. Win-Daled was by far the greatest Arch-mage in the nation, and she had the mighty elven Ye'Cind and the great Flan wunderkind Heward as friends and advisors. 
 The Singing One and the Flan roguish  warrior were fond of wandering though, and lately had been frequenting Risewater less and less. Ye'Cind was still a young elf maiden and Heward seemed to have stopped aging at forty.
    Win-Daled herself felt old, and she was ready to move on to the next stage of existence.She had hoped Heward would take up the job...oh well...his dalliances with the nymphs, dryads and other feminine creatures of Fey was apparently taking up too much of his time for serious work.
    Therefore, Win-Daled chose the son of a gallant former bandit to be her successor. Gryman was intelligent, contemplative and had earned the respect of many of the young Suel in his twenty three years. He was deeply moved by the honour, and promised to serve the Suel faithfully and fairly. Win-Daled assured him that she knew he would.
   At the end of the year, after giving a last speech and wishing everybody well, Win-Daled clutched her heart and fell back on the stage. Her face was serene, and her lips curved with the hint of a smile. She never rose again.
   52 SD, Ye'Cind finally joined up with a small grey elf community that had splintered off from Celene and helped to found a new Elven nation north of the Vast swamp.
   55 SD, Heward, galavanting about Fey, crossed paths with a band of jealous satyrs while in the company of a vivacious nymph. They struck him down and placed him in a  magical prison. There he remained for a long, long time... See less

A History of Oerik
Book 1 
Part 49
155 SD
   So many factors created the split between the growing Suloise settlements of South western Oerik that it is impossible to convey it all in a short history of this nature.  Suel living near mines got rich and nearly everyone else got progressively poorer.  Bandits proliferated.  Rivalry festered. The Suelchief of Risewater was not recognised as superior to the Suelchief of Emeraldglare (though he considered it obviously so), and the Suelchief of Rockfern decided that she was the superior one (for her wisdom was legendary), and all else must pay a tithe in homage to her. 
  Yet, a significant number of Suel thought that Thurnfedge III, as Great Grandson of Thurnfedge I, appointed by Win-Daled herself, surely had the ascendency.  
    Each town, farm and barracks had their own loyalties.  Orcs, orogs, gnolls, norkers and ogres took advantage of the divisions and made many successful raids upon the furthest outposts.  
   Some Suel took the opportunity of becoming mercenaries to anyone who looked strongest on the day, including the humanoids.Half orcs and half ogres appeared in Oerik for the first time.  
   Political differences also had a part in the rupture. Seasonal food shortages meant some wished to trade with their ancient elvish enemies of the East, the Singing Ones.Others wanted more trade with the dwarves and humanoids. Arguments and fights broke out between neighbours.  Magic, religions and differing laws all added to the feuding.  
   Sorcery was banned in Emeraldglare but encouraged in Risewater.  Rockfern introduced slavery to punish transgressors, and consequently  Risewater Suel raised farms and crops in protest.  Inevitably full blown wars broke out.  
   Emeraldglare  had the best access to copper and tin, and they were sure they would subjugate their enemies. 
   Rockfern were disciplined and blessed with well drilled troops, so victory was there for the taking.
    Risewater had a lesser army and less metal resources, but they had the best weapon of all, because they had the gods on their side. Let their foes tremble before them!
   By the end of 155 SD the Suel, after terrible battles with much loss of life, divided into two major entities: the Holy Papacy of Risewater and the Noble Highhold of Emeraldrock. See less

A History of Oerik
Book 1 
Part 52
   The Jann had lived in the west over the Darkwalll mountains for thousands of years. 
    Related to the Wind Dukes far away in the northeast, they worshipped and embraced the Four Great Elements.  To this end they built magnificent Temple Cities out of Elemental Shadestone where they held short ceremonies four times a day.  
   Their land was semi-arid but they had all they needed, for the beating sun nourished them with Fire, the rocky landscape nourished with Earth, the breeze nourished them with Air and the underground springs nourished with Water.
    The trade with the Highhold Suel opened up exciting new paths. Trade with other neighbours had proved to be impossible as the  humanoid tribes were aggressive, particularly the mantis Thri Kreen.
   Trade with the Suloiise led to some Jann travelling easy and exploring the human realms. Taller than most Suel, with piercing eyes, multiple skin colours,  billowing violet robes and powerful magic, the jann proved to be an intimidating and threatening presence to many Highholders, creating some friction. Yet, it was the  Suel of the Holy Papacy that were least tolerant, the Pope declaring the elementals infidels, and banished their presence from the Theocracy.
     This did not stop a fair few open minded and adventurous Suel  from crossing west and coexisting with the Jann in their own beautiful cities.
    Despite the ups and downs, trading between the two peoples continued to enrich both and this windfall changed both cultures irrevocably. 
    Individual Jann and Suel grew in power and influence separating themselves from the traditional classes and castes that anchored the majority. Highholders who had missed out on owning the mines from the lucky First Families now could get very rich very quickly. 
   There were Jann, too, who found themselves attracted to Suel culture, dressing in  Suel clothes and utilising Suel words.
   All were watched, and all were judged. See less

A History of Oerik
Book 1 
Part 53
189 SD
   The Jann paid a high price for their dalliances with the Suel.
   Skin cracked and opened up into ulcerating sores, eyes seeped puss, teeth crumbled and bones dissolved to sand. Who was punishing them so?
   It was their own gods, the  Elemental Princes, hurling punishments upon their followers in righteous wrath.*
     How dare the Jann, the Holy Jann, holders of the Material Elements, betray their heritage and inheritance?  
   Those Jann who had not lapsed, watched their forsaken brothers and sisters suffer and did nothing.  The Suel watched on in terror. 
 . One in twelve Jann succumbed in this way.  No magic could Cure or Raise them for the Elemental Princes had no mercy.  
   Alas the Jann were not free! Their fate during the long Dragon Wars in the Lost Age led them to be bonded with the elements for evermore. 
    Bound in ritual and worship as part of the Celestial Covenant, their destiny was as unbreakable as their shadestone. 
   Across the mountains far to the north east,  their kin, the Wind Dukes loved the order and law and grew strong in their righteous Observance.
    Oh pity the Jann!  Their path on Oerth had led them into Questioning their required Place.  They were vulnerable to moral decay and physical destruction.
   The Suel of  Highhold were not  passed by without consequence either.  A series of earthquakes brought down a mountain,  crushing thousands.  Great tempests brought floods followed by lightning storms that ignited fires in the villages and farms.  
   The beautiful bastille of Risewater tumbled down, followed by storms and fires that left death and devastation in long corridors of destruction.
*Their beliefs, not mine! See less

A History of Oerik
Book 1 
Part 54
   The apostates of Emeraldrock had unleashed elemental Hell upon the Suel, and they would pay! 
   The bronze of her armour blazing in the sunlight, Pope Syrul strode out into the town square then called out her Holy subjects. They must take up arms against the Highholders and destroy them.
   Syrul  gestured towards the sundered bastille, the greatest fortress ever built, laid low as a result of the Highholders meddling.  Was there fear in the eyes of the crowd? Yes, but more for the fear of her than the fear of war.  Pope Syrul  was known to break the legs of those who misinterpreted her commands.
   So it was that the Holy Papacy of Risewater marched yet again on their former comrades. The Highholders had suffered even more than Risewater and had no desire for battle. With the destruction of their mines, the First Families had lost the source of their power. Unable to control their people, lawlessness had broken out, the farmers and miners now brigands and bandits.
   The papists fell upon Emeraldrock. Once famed, the Highhold army was in turmoil, the few soldiers left completely outnumbered  by the invaders.  
    Emeraldrock was quickly conquered but Syrul found there was no subsequent control, for the banditry was indemic.
   Risewater bishops  were brought in to quell the chaos.Holy Wizards they were, with the teachings of legendary Win-Daled resonating within their heads 
   Unfortunately for the Pope, the bishops brought dismay upon Emeraldrock but achieved little  The lands had been burned by the Elementals and nothing would grow, and the mines were completely buried by the broken mountain.
   Turning away from the destruction, Pope Syrul then ordered her forces to penetrate the Darkwall mountains and deal a lesson to the Jann, the abominations who had brought this hardship to the Suloiise... See less

A History of Oerik
Book 1 
Part 55
   Breaking through the pass of the Darkwall mountains was grueling and costly.  Bandits, gnolls and orcs swarmed the open areas and had plenty of hidden holes to retreat and emerge from.  Syrup realised that her Papal army was losing numbers too quickly.  
   The magical Bishops desperately punched into the Jann enclave eventually , but guarding the city was a gigantic blue skinned, scimitar wielding Djinn,  with elemental servants of all types around her, and the Jann as well.
     The upshot was that Pope Syrul's  army was soundly defeated.  The surviving Bishops and soldiers were enslaved and taken North East to the Wind Dukes.
   When the news reached the Pope, she wisely withdrew from attacking her foes and concentrated on defence. 
    Bandits, orcs and Highhold forces raided and tested the Papists,  so Syrulreached out for Divine power  by exhorting all the Risewater civilians to attend the temples and offer gifts and prayers to the Goddess.  
   Did the Goddess manifest herself and wreak bloody vengeance upon the enemy?  No, not exactly, but Pope Syrul and her four Cardinals claimed that the blasts of energy smiting their foes was  Divine Wrath.
   Over and over, pink and scarlet fire erupted out from the stomachs of the invaders, whether orc, bandit or Highholder.  Their comrades writhing and burning into ash, fear overcame the  remaining raiders, and they fled. 
   Syrul breathed a sigh of relief. The Holy Papacy of Risewater was still intact, though barely. See less

198 SD
   Thurnfedge V absently stroked the whip on his lap, the whip taken by Win-Daled from Dweomyne, and the symbol of his legitimate right to rule.
     Norebo looked into the eyes of his king with barely concealed contempt.  Thurnfedge V had watery eyes, devoid of colour. His teeth were clenched and his nose leaked.It was unfortunate that thenoble line had ended up with him. At least he was easily impressed by others, and he fortunately doted upon the sleek Thief Merchant standing before him.
   "Then what is to be done?" asked Thurnfedge helplessly.
   Thurnfedge never knew what was to be done.
    Norebo sighed and pushed a lock of dark hair away from his brow.
   "Leave it with me," he said.  
   In fact, Norebo was not overly concerned with the collapse of the economy in Emeraldrock (which they had been discussing). With Highhold in chaos, and with the Holy Papacy hanging tenuously to its borders, it was going to get pretty rough....
   Norebo knew that his  prosperity was secure, because he was a member of the Oath, a secret society based in the Eastern kingdoms.on the coast of the Solnor sea. The Oath had feelers everywhere. Most of the bandit companies were Oath members, and there were even a handful of Lowly Ones in the Singing Lands who were Brothers.  
   The major Thief Houses were all Oathers, and lucrative trade passed easily between them. The lands around could be poor, but the Oath Society was only increasing its wealth. 
   Norebo knew this, because he was the Merchant Prince overseeing it all.  
   Originally from the east, Norebo had a way of blending in with the Suloise, even with his coppery skin and dark hair. His subtle magic allowed him to be accepted everywhere.. 
   In actuality, Norebo was not concerned about anything much, he found life easy and enjoyable. It was fun to rule behind the scenes watching money flow into Oather coffers. The trick was to stay in the shadows and let the ignorant do the work. See less

Part 57
200 SD
   Ye'Cind had been enjoying her life in Sunndi.  She had been appointed to the Elder Council despite her youth, as a result of her experience and magical ability. 
   She was wise and understood the needs of the Flan, elves, dwarves, gnomes and halflings that made Sunndi their home. She had not yet married despite pressure from others to do so.  Frankly she had yet to find somebody interesting enough to live with, so she chose the solitary life.
   Ye'Cind frequently travelled abroad.  She was a Singing One elf and that land still drew upon her, dark though it was.
  The Singing Lands had retreated from demonology, but  tens of thousands of Lowly Ones were still enslaved. There was a new cultural interest in the big wide world, with various Singing One traders, adventurers and artists often seen on the road.
   Travelling singers would move all around Eastern Oerik, from Celene, to Blemu and the eastern Flannish kingdoms.  Ye'Cind liked their singing and who wouldn't?  Their voices were supernatural. 
 Ye'Cind could not sing like her fellows. It felt to her that her complete failure to hold a note was  a result of her mind being wired very differently to the other Singing Ones. She thought with a calm but deep intelligence, and unlike her kin, was filled with compassion for others. Naturally she would then be cursed with a voice of wayward pitch. 
She was a great mimic though, and could imitate nearly any sound she had ever heard, so  long it was harsh and grating. She was also a natural musician, and could make beautiful sounds from the most unlikely materials.
   So, Ye'Cind regularly went to hear Singing One minstrels whenever they came to Sunndi,  listening with admiration and not a little jealousy. See less

A History of Oerik
Book 1
Part 58
202 SD
   Emeraldrock broke into eight states each ruled by a High Chief and each guarded by a tower and keep. 
   The Holy Papacy of Risewater was as if an island, surrounded by a sea of bandits, humanoids and mercenaries.  
   The elves of the Singing Ones built and prepared for invasion.
   The secret Oath Society was behind it all.
   For the High Chiefs were all Oathers.  Money flowed in from Oathers and out to Oathers. The population hated the bandits, or the Papacy, or the High Chiefs, or the Singing Ones, but it didn't matter, the Oathers were everywhere.
   Mines were reopened, armies were equipped and trained.
   In Risewater the Papacy was firmly under the religion of  the Goddess as interpreted by Pope Syrul, but what she didn't know was that much of the soldiery she employed were secretly Oathers.
In the Singing Lands  key Lowly Ones were Oathers and spied for Thurnfedge V and his adviser Norebo. Bandits counted Oathers amongst their numbers.
   Soon the Suloise nations would implode and the Oathers would openly install Thurnfedge V ruling over His people as was His right. See less

Part 59
The swords pointed at Pope Syrul's heart looked very sharp. Syrul decided to play it cool.
   "And what can I do for you?" Syrul asked nonchalantly.. 
   Behind the hostile guards, a sleek young man with dark hair pushed forward.
   "Dear Holy one, your rule is over," said the man in a kindly yet firm tone. "My name is Norebo, and I represent the true Suloise heir, Thurnfedge V.  Your soldiers now answer only to me."
   Thurnfedge?  Mused Syrul. A spindly, stupid runt now in charge of the Suel people? Hardly! Something else was going on. 
  "Why all this hostility?" Asked Syrul, "I am on your side, as is the Goddess. I beg of you, please put those swords away." 
   "I regret that I cannot do that."
    "The Goddess created Thurnfedge. She chose him."
 One of the guards grew impatient and his sword touched her blouse. Syrul stood very still 
   "So, I take it, " said Norebo "that you do indeed accept Thurnfedge V as the ruler of Risewater and the other Suloise realms,"
   Pope Syrul explained that she, as the Pope was merely an empty vessel filled by the grace of the Goddess. If the Goddess allowed Thurnfedge V to rule the entirety of the Suloiise people, then she would naturally acquiesce.
